sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a fixed-length micro panel with finite group and covariate supports.
sampling_model.treatment: Group one is untreated through \(T-1\) and treated only in period \(T\); every donor group remains untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \((G,X)\) cell has probability bounded away from zero by the displayed margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell probabilities and group-time means make every profiled normal and covariance program computable. Fixed-coordinate plug-in charts admit a sequencewise \(O(n^{-1/2})\) \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) continuation along each fixed branch-local sequence, where the constant may depend on that sequence. The frozen sequence class does not authorize a uniformly valid data-driven branch selection, one-step estimator, variance estimator, or multiplier interval.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 uses the same time-invariant covariate-indexed mean representation, and Theorems 2--4 give separate PT and SC limit and multiplier laws under the maintained branch.
Theorem 3.1 gives covariance-optimal PT weighting in the overidentified short-panel DiD model.
Section 3 constructs an intersection-efficient union-model estimator for a different finite-support odds-ratio problem.
Proposition 1 derives the semiparametric efficiency bound for the two-group panel-DiD ATT.

The paper gives cross-fit remainder theory for smooth average linear functionals under common rate control; it does not validate uniformity over a sequence class closed under finite-coordinate replacement.
Sections 3--4 analyze drift under branchwise nuisance validity, but do not remove the finite-coordinate-splicing obstruction in the frozen local-sequence class.

body.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification remains valid when either conditional parallel trends or a uniquely identified full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction holds. At an intersection law, profiling the latent PT counterfactual change exposes two affine influence classes whose intersection yields a computable union convolution bound. The equal-share three-group witness has \(V_{\mathrm{PT}}=42/5\), \(V_{\mathrm{SC}}=1625/184\), and \(V_U=39/4\), with respective union costs \(27/20\) and \(169/184\). The adaptation frontier is positive only sequencewise: along each fixed root-\(n\) branch sequence the active-chart score continues at \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) distance \(O(n^{-1/2})\), with a sequence-dependent constant. Uniform one-step and multiplier attainment over the frozen sequence class is false because finite-coordinate splicing can assign distinct admissible chart labels to the same observed law.

project_justification.gap: SunXieZhang2025 identifies the ATT under PT or SC but proves distinct branchwise influence and bootstrap results; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives the PT efficiency bound alone. Neither source determines the regular influence class or convolution lower bound for the nonconvex union at an intersection law.
project_justification.niche: Finite covariate support makes the \(J\) treated-versus-donor PT equalities and the full-rank SC restriction finite-dimensional. Profiling the latent treated counterfactual coordinate exposes their observed normal geometry, so the efficiency loss and adaptation frontier reduce to observable covariance algebra.
project_justification.fill: The project profiles the PT restriction, characterizes both branch influence faces, computes their minimum-norm intersection by finite covariance-weighted programs, gives observable simultaneous and one-sided adaptation tests, and supplies a strict quantitative three-group witness. It also resolves the attainment frontier: branch-valid score continuation survives along every fixed local sequence, but the frozen class cannot support one estimator with a uniform asymptotic-linear or multiplier guarantee. A positive uniform theorem would require a genuinely common local neighborhood, common score and remainder bounds, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.

body.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor. Its synthetic-control hypothesis uses one time-invariant, covariate-indexed group-weight vector for all untreated period means, exactly as in \(\mathrm{ass{:}synthetic\text{-}mean}\). The intercept row of \(B(x)\) imposes \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}w(x)=1\). Subtracting a reference-donor column from the other donor columns shows that \(\operatorname{rank}B(x)=J\) is equivalent to invertibility of the published reference-difference matrix \(M(x)^{\prime}M(x)\). Finite covariate support together with uniform interior cell, overlap, moment, and rank margins makes the present class a regular finite-support subclass of that published model. Therefore lower bounds and impossibility results apply to every estimator regular on the broader published union by restriction to this subclass, while sharpness is claimed only locally on the stated full-rank subclass. SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, supplies separate branchwise limit and multiplier laws; it does not supply a uniform law across the frozen branch-switching sequence class. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting, while the present analysis profiles all treated-versus-donor equalities before intersecting the PT and SC influence faces. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different finite-support union problem. SantAnnaZhao2020 supplies the single-donor panel-DiD benchmark. NeweyRobins2018 and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 motivate cross-fit and branchwise remainder control, but neither excludes finite-coordinate replacement; accordingly they support the sequencewise continuation, not an affirmative uniform theorem. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska application in SunXieZhang2025 are the motivating empirical consumers.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The union bound is local and regular at an intersection law with fixed overlap, support, moment, rank, and spectral margins. Sharpness is not claimed at SC rank failure, vanishing overlap, changing covariate support, covariance degeneracy, or on the broader published model away from this finite-support full-rank subclass. The sequencewise chart continuation is not uniform: its constant may depend on the fixed sequence, and the frozen class permits finite-coordinate replacements that preclude a common estimator expansion and multiplier coupling.
body.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are branchwise tangent-normal forms at regular intersection centers, the finite-program union convolution envelope, simultaneous and one-sided oracle-adaptation criteria, the strict three-group constants \(V_{\mathrm{PT}}=42/5\), \(V_{\mathrm{SC}}=1625/184\), and \(V_U=39/4\), and the single-donor reduction. A branch-valid active-chart score also continues along every fixed root-\(n\) sequence at \(O(n^{-1/2})\) \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) distance, with a sequence-dependent constant. Uniform asymptotic linearity, variance consistency, branch coupling, and multiplier coverage over the frozen sequence class are false by finite-coordinate splicing. A positive uniform result would need a common neighborhood, common score and remainder bounds, and a sequence class excluding finite-coordinate replacement. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer to estimators regular on the broader Sun--Xie--Zhang union by subclass restriction; local sharpness remains limited to the stated full-rank finite-support class.
